issue_note: research-state.yaml's H4 entry says 'issue #30' -- that number was already taken by the raytun3r thread's ticket 028-da3-row-and-the-papers-span.md (README also lists it as (#30)); the real corresponding issue is #31 ('Do hand/body pixels disrupt pose, and should the head ignore them?').
protocol_notes: 40 pose pairs and up to 41 single-frame anchors per sequence, evenly spread across the whole sequence (not literally adjacent 30Hz frames) -- 'consecutive-ish' read as adjacent within the evenly-spaced anchor list, not within the raw capture stream.
GT relative pose: get_aria_3d_pose_by_timestamp_ns, conjugated device->camera by issue #27's audited T_device_camera quaternion -- no hand-eye bootstrap.

Camera intrinsics/distortion: this repo's existing Aria KB4 model (cam3r.cameras.aria_214_1_kb4 + raytun3r.cameras.KannalaBrandt), matching adt_pose_value.py/feature_head.py; the calibration JSON supplies only the device<->camera rotation.
Dynamic-pixel mask: same InstanceType.HUMAN segmentation method as ticket 028's hand_pixel_stats.py, resized to 504x504 (nearest) alongside a bicubic-resized RGB frame.

random_matched mask: per-frame pixel count equal to that frame's own dynamic-pixel count, drawn uniformly from the cone, seeded per pair -- not patch-aligned (masking here is mean-fill preprocessing, not token dropping, so pixel-level granularity is fine).
Depth arm's static AbsRel uses scale_shift alignment (finetune.eval.metrics.align_depth), range domain, matching the H2.1/H2.2 protocol of record.

read.verdict: the prediction (GT-dynamic masking beats an area-matched random mask on high-dyn_frac pairs) is only weakly and inconsistently supported: positive on 2/3 sequences at ~0.3-1.0 deg against baseline errors of 10-25 deg, a wash on the third, and the depth arm shows no consistent gain from removing hands from the input (1/3 sequences improved, 2/3 slightly worse). Closer to (b) ~ (c) than to a clear win for GT masking -- hands read more like occlusion than like a distinct source of signal corruption at this scale, so H4 leans toward 'the head should skip dynamic cells in its loss' rather than needing dynamic-aware input correction. Not read as decisive given only 3 sequences and 7-30 high-dyn_frac pairs per sequence.
